items.title: Willie Hightower Interview, 1958-06-03
items.q: With the backing of Annole Matoia. See, as I told you, I'd been taken from him. And I agreed to take the show out, if Annole would go on the show, because I couldn't handle it.

ctx.x: Can't think of old man's Parks' initials. But anyhow, it was afterwards, C.W. Parks. C.W. Parks. Then, we got together and I signed a contract to take a band on this show. With the backing of Annole Matoia. See, as I told you, I'd been taken from him. And I agreed to take the show out, if Annole would go on the show, because I couldn't handle it. Because the show was to have a hundred people on it.

items.title: Willie Hightower Interview, 1958-06-03
items.q: So I played down there one night in his place practically all night.

ctx.x: Some pictures I've seen of him, he looks a little bit like Peter Boccage.

Yeah, well, you wouldn't know whether he was a white or what he was, see. But, at those, just around that time he was turning, he was turning to that wine, that drinking, see. One of the greatest trumpet players that ever was. He played with number one Ringling Brothers band, the white band. He sat in the band. And when Zoo carried me there, he always says, a trumpet player? So and so was the case, and he passed me on the show, he said, come on, sit down, here's my horn. That just gave him a chance to go walk…
